ticket.title: Stop browsers and proxies caching comment listings and single comments
ticket.description: Readers sometimes see a stale list of comments because a browser or a proxy cached the JSON the comment widget fetched. The two read endpoints that return comments, the thread listing and the single-comment view, must tell every cache not to store their successful responses. Error responses and the other endpoints are not changed.
contract: `GET /?uri=<uri>` (the comment listing of a thread): every response with a status below 400 carries the header `Cache-Control: no-store`, exactly that value. This holds with any of the endpoint's query parameters (`sort`, `limit`, `offset`, `parent`, `nested_limit`, `plain`, `after`).

`GET /id/<id>` (one comment, readable by the client holding that comment's edit cookie, which `POST /new` sets under the cookie name `<id>`): a 200 response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`, exactly that value. `?plain=1` makes no difference.

Responses with a status of 400 or above from these two endpoints get no `Cache-Control` header from this change: for example `GET /?uri=<uri>&sort=bogus` (400), `GET /id/<id>` for a missing comment (404), and `GET /id/<id>` without the edit cookie (403).
No other route changes: `POST /new`, `PUT /id/<id>`, `DELETE /id/<id>`, `POST /count`, `GET /latest`, `GET /config` and the rest keep their headers as they were.
Response bodies and status codes of both endpoints are unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: After a comment is posted on a thread, GET /?uri=<that thread> returns 200 with the header Cache-Control: no-store
The comment's author, using the edit cookie from POST /new, gets 200 from GET /id/<id> with the header Cache-Control: no-store
GET /?uri=<thread>&sort=bogus returns 400 without a Cache-Control: no-store header
GET /id/<id> for a comment that does not exist returns 404 without a Cache-Control: no-store header
The JSON bodies of GET /?uri=<thread> and GET /id/<id> are the same as before the change
